title: बझाङी लोकगीतको अध्ययन Bajhangi Lokgeetko Adhyayan
nepali: यस लेखमा बझाङमा गाइने लोकगीतहरूमा सांख्य, वेदान्त दर्शन, अलङ्कार, गुण, रीति, अमिधा, लक्षणा, व्यञ्जना, रस, भाव जस्ता साहित्यका उत्कृष्ट तइभ्वले विभूषित भएका देखिन्छन् । यिनमा नै सङ्गतिको श्रुतिमनोहर माधुर्यता भरिएको छ । अनेक लय तथा तालका साथ यीं लोकगीतको संयोग भएपछि कर्णप्रिय हुन्छन् । यीं लोकगीतहरू स्तरीय काव्यकृतिहरूभन्दा कम छैन भन्ने कुराको विश्लेषण गर्न खोजिएको छ । बझाङी लोकगीतहरूलाई कालिदासका प्रमुख कृतिहरूसंग भाव सामिप्यता रहेको देखिन्छ भन्ने कुरालाई केही उदाहरण दिएर स्पष्ट गर्ने प्रयास गरिएको छ ।
american_english: In this article, the folk songs sung in Bajhang are seen to be adorned with excellent elements of literature such as Sankhya and Vedanta philosophy, figures of speech, qualities, styles, denotation, indication, suggestion, rasa, and bhava. In them, the pleasing sweetness of sound in verbal harmony is also filled. When these folk songs are combined with many rhythms and beats, they become pleasing to the ear. An attempt has been made to analyze the point that these folk songs are not inferior to high-quality poetic works. An effort has been made to clarify, by giving some examples, the point that the folk songs of Bajhang are seen to have an affinity of sentiment with the major works of Kalidasa.

informal_english: In this article, the folk songs sung in Bajhang are seen to be decked out with some top-notch elements of literature like Sankhya and Vedanta philosophy, figures of speech, qualities, styles, denotation, indication, suggestion, rasa, and bhava. On top of that, they’re filled with the really sweet, musical sound of verbal harmony. When you mix these folk songs in with a bunch of different rhythms and beats, they’re super easy on the ears. The article tries to make the case that these folk songs are no less than high-quality poetic works. It also tries to show, by giving a few examples, that the folk songs of Bajhang seem to have a real closeness of feeling with the major works of Kalidasa.
translator_notes: The source text contains an apparent OCR artifact ('तइभ्वले'); it was translated in context as 'elements' to preserve the intended meaning while keeping sentence order intact. Sanskrit-derived literary terms (rasa, bhava) were retained as established loan terms.
